questions.text: Define energy signal and power signal with mathematical expressions and examples. Determine whether the signal $x(t) = e^{-at}u(t)$ for $a > 0$ (or $x(t) = 5\cos(t)$) is an energy signal, power signal, or neither, and calculate its total energy or average power.

Show that any arbitrary continuous or discrete time signal can be decomposed into an even component and an odd component ($x(t) = x_e(t) + x_o(t)$). Find and sketch the even and odd components of a given signal.
Explain time shifting, time scaling, and time reversal (reflection) operations on continuous-time and discrete-time signals with neat graphical illustrations.
Derive the necessary condition for a discrete-time complex exponential signal $x[n] = e^{j\omega_0 n}$ to be periodic. What is its fundamental period $N$?

questions.chapter: Fourier Analysis of Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Signals
questions.text: State and prove Parseval's relation for: (a) Continuous-Time Fourier Series, and (b) Discrete-Time Fourier Series (DTFS).

questions.chapter: Fourier Analysis of Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Signals
questions.text: Find the Continuous-Time Fourier Transform (CTFT) of the signal $x(t) = e^{-at}u(t)$ for $a > 0$. Plot its magnitude and phase spectrum.

questions.chapter: Fourier Analysis of Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Signals
questions.text: State and prove the Convolution property of the Continuous-Time Fourier Transform: $\mathcal{F}\{x_1(t) * x_2(t)\} = X_1(j\omega) X_2(j\omega)$.

questions.chapter: Fourier Analysis of Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Signals
questions.text: State and prove the Duality property and Time-Scaling property of the Continuous-Time Fourier Transform.
Derive the Convolution Integral for a continuous-time Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) system: $y(t) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty x(\tau)h(t-\tau)d\tau$.

Derive the Convolution Sum for a discrete-time LTI system: $y[n] = \sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty x[k]h[n-k]$. Find and plot the convolution sum of sequences $x[n] = \{1, 3, 4, 3, 1\}$ and $h[n] = \{2, 2, -2\}$ (or $x[n] = \{3, 1, 5\}$ and $h[n] = \{1, 4, -2, 3\}$).

Define an LTI system and explain fundamental system properties: Linearity, Time-Invariance, Causality, Memory, and BIBO Stability. State the condition for an LTI system to be causal and stable in terms of impulse response.

State and prove the Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem using frequency-domain analysis. Define Nyquist rate and Nyquist interval. What is aliasing and how is it prevented? Determine the Nyquist rate for $x(t) = \cos(200\pi t) + \sin(400\pi t)$.

Derive formula to calculate the impulse response of an Ideal Low-Pass Filter in continuous/discrete time. Prove, with necessary mathematical derivations, that an ideal low-pass filter is non-causal and physically unrealizable.

questions.chapter: Fourier Analysis of Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Signals
questions.text: Derive the synthesis and analysis equations of the Discrete-Time Fourier Transform (DTFT). State and prove the Linearity, Time-Shifting, and Frequency-Shifting properties of DTFT.

questions.chapter: Fourier Analysis of Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Signals
questions.text: Compute the 4-point Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) for the sequence $x[n] = \{3, -2, 1, 4\}$ using the twiddle factor matrix $W_N^{kn}$.
For a system characterized by a linear constant coefficient difference equation, determine the frequency response $H(e^{j\omega})$ and impulse response $h[n]$. Plot the magnitude and phase response.
